headline: A fast-moving coastal storm brings a soaking 1–3 inches of rain and some wind to New York City and the region Sunday afternoon into Monday morning, with another coastal storm possible Wednesday night into Thanksgiving.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: High pressure keeps Friday evening and night dry and quiet around New York City. Winds stay light, under about 10 mph, and go calm in most areas outside the city by early evening. No watches, warnings or advisories are in effect.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Saturday stays dry, with light winds turning east to southeast in the afternoon. A low-pressure system moving up the coast brings rain starting as soon as early Sunday afternoon, with the heaviest Sunday night as the storm passes over or just southeast of eastern Long Island; expect 1–2 inches across the region and a stripe of close to 3 inches somewhere over Long Island, southern Connecticut and possibly New York City, where rain could fall at more than half an inch per hour for several hours, plus a few possible thunderstorms. Because the storm moves quickly, the main risk is minor flooding of streets, small streams and poorly drained areas rather than widespread flash flooding. If the storm's center crosses Long Island, eastern Long Island and southeast Connecticut could see south-southeast gusts of 45–55 mph Sunday night (with a few north gusts to 40 mph farther west), and rain lingers early Monday before improving in the afternoon with northwest to west gusts around 25–30 mph.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Tuesday is dry with weakening north-northwest winds, and Wednesday looks dry during the day. Another coastal storm is possible Wednesday night into Thanksgiving Day: the main European and American models take it well offshore, southeast of Nantucket, which would limit strong winds to eastern Long Island and Connecticut, but many of the stronger model scenarios track it closer, bringing more direct impacts and a wider wind threat along the coast.

coast: Coastal flooding from Sunday night's storm looks minimal because the Monday morning high tide comes after the storm passes, with winds blowing offshore, though rough seas offshore slow drainage from the back bays and a few Long Island south shore spots could approach or reach minor flood levels. The Wednesday night–Thanksgiving storm comes right after Tuesday's full moon, so at least widespread minor coastal flooding is possible even if it stays offshore, and the reasonable worst case is moderate flooding over several high tides Wednesday into Friday. On the water, at least small-craft-advisory conditions are expected on all waters Sunday night, lingering on the ocean afterward in northwest winds; gales are possible on the ocean, eastern Long Island Sound and the bays Sunday night depending on the storm's track (a Gale Watch may become necessary), and on all waters Wednesday night.
watch_for: Where the heaviest rain sets up Sunday night: close to 3 inches possible over Long Island, southern Connecticut and possibly NYC, with minor street and small-stream flooding.

confidence: Forecasters made no significant changes and models look similar on Sunday–Monday's rain, though its winds depend on the exact track; the Thanksgiving storm's track and impacts are still uncertain.
